challenge.method: Split the publisher text at the start of clause 1. Lowercased each compared text and extracted ordered runs of ASCII letters and digits. Tested passage token equality, raw byte equality and full-file token equality, then verified the identifier and tag target.
challenge.results: Publisher bytes [0, 306) contain the same 41 ordered tokens as each complete 268-byte SPDX representation, from `no` through `license`. Both byte comparisons fail due to indentation, blank-line layout and the period after SPDX's clause number. The full publisher file has 44 tokens because bytes [306, 317) add `1`, `goto`, `0`. Both SPDX paths are pinned to the annotated tag's target.

limitations: The correspondence covers tokens through clause 0 in the pinned historical form. The full project variant includes clause 1. Other forms, legal equivalence and unstated software releases are outside scope.
The API records the tag as unsigned, so provenance rests on the pinned repository routes and connector capture.
reasoning: The tag, identifier and ordered token comparisons support the specified passage correspondence. The byte and full-file differences confirm the edition boundary stated in the claim.
